A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDCP research work. The main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original classification and regression simulations and experiments on FMoW, PovertyMap and MEPS. Appendix D includes additional optimization and distribution-shift experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds oracle comparisons, randomization experiments, runtime measurements and scaling results.

M1.justification: The implemented MDCP procedure retains per-source density estimation, learned nonnegative dual weights, max-p aggregation and regression grid search. Algorithms 1–2 remain substantively unchanged; the new randomization comparisons examine variants of the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic classification/regression families, including covariate and concept shifts, and the same FMoW, PovertyMap and MEPS populations. The new scaling studies vary sample counts, source counts and balance within the retained data-generating processes.

E2.justification: v2 adds an Oracle comparator using ground-truth conditional densities for dual-weight learning and score calculation, evaluated in Figures 2–7 and the scaling tables. The source-specific and naive max-p baselines remain, and real-data comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds controlled sweeps over total sample size 1500–6000, source counts 2/3/5/10 and balance ratios 1/2/4/8, plus runtime measurements separated into five computational stages. It also compares randomized p-values with fixed U=0 and U=1. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained penalty-tuning and distribution-shift studies, v2 investigates density-estimation error using Oracle, tie randomization, runtime bottlenecks and sensitivity to sample size, source count and imbalance. However, regression randomization Figures 24–25 duplicate classification Figures 21–22, leaving those two claimed regression cases unsupported by distinct plots.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions or random splits, with per-run dots and, where applicable, bands showing one standard deviation. The added experiments extend this reporting practice without introducing different run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds Oracle results and extensive coverage, set-size and runtime entries in Tables 1–12. For example, Table 1's balanced linear classification setting reports runtimes of 7.1 seconds for Baseline-agg and 53.3 seconds for MDCP. The original real-data, penalty-tuning and covariate-shift plots are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 replaces v1's Levy-distance quantile lemma with a stricter horizontal-CDF-sandwich condition and revises its proof. Theorem 3 specifies almost-sure boundedness, and Appendix C.4 adds a sufficient grid-resolution condition. The principal optimality and sieve results are retained, often relocated or renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: finite-sample uniform coverage without test-source labels, optimality and tightness with appropriate scores, and efficient classification/regression implementations. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement explicitly distinguishes population coverage from protection for individual predictions and discusses reduced utility when calibration data for a source are scarce. New discussion interprets oracle gaps and identifies dual-weight optimization, particularly in classification, as the computational bottleneck.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies Adam's learning rate, minibatch size, 10,000-epoch cap, stopping tolerances and density clipping. Appendix C.5.1 discloses FMoW head sharing. These improve implementation documentation; the code repository remains the same, despite its relocated reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds targeted comparisons with Duchi et al. on multi-environment inference, Tibshirani et al. on covariate shift, and prediction-set volume optimization work. Some general uncertainty-quantification and future-work citations are removed. The fundamental positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially condensed and reorganized. Full related work, sieve theory, Algorithm 1, simulation specifications and detailed application descriptions move into Appendices A and C. The discussion becomes a short conclusion, with separate reproducibility and impact statements.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text with substantially smaller plots, redraws Figures 2–7 to include Oracle, and adds randomization/runtime displays and twelve tables. Existing covariate-shift Figures 20–23 become Figures 26–29. The new regression-captioned Figures 24–25 incorrectly reuse classification plots.

improvement.justification: The oracle comparisons, scaling/runtime evidence, explicit optimizer settings and localized proof correction strengthen the evaluation and reproducibility beyond v1's already substantial treatment. The net gain is limited by duplicated classification plots presented as regression results in Figures 24–25 and reduced readability of the compressed main-text figures.
